title: 5 Proven Growth Hacks to Skyrocket Your App’s Downloads and Revenue
summary: Unlock these effective strategies for app growth, from apps-gone-free campaigns to App Store features — all backed by real-world success examples.
body_text: In today's competitive market, standing out and driving downloads is more challenging than ever. But, it's also never been more important. Whether you're launching a new game, a productivity tool, or an innovative service, you need some strategies in place to break through the noise. Drawing from years of experience studying the app space while heading up App Masters and Indie App Santa, here are five of the most effective growth hacking strategies that I've seen. 1. Rethinking the apps gone free campaign One of the classic growth hacking techniques is the apps-gone-free campaign. Traditionally, this involves temporarily converting a paid app to free status for a limited period to create a surge of downloads. In today's landscape, this approach can be tweaked for modern monetization models. Instead of switching a paid app completely free, you can strategically offer a non-consumable in-app purchase (IAP) for free for a couple of days. Typically, the remove ads IAP works well for games whereas the lifetime IAP works better for subscription-based apps. By making a premium feature available at no cost for a limited time, you create urgency among potential users. The free offer acts as a powerful incentive — people who might hesitate to pay for premium features are now more willing to at least try the app. With increased downloads during this "promotional" period, many developers have seen not only a boost in user numbers, but also a significant increase in subsequent in-app purchases. Making more sales during an apps-gone-free campaign than in several months of standard operation. — An App Masters client For example, one client we tried this with even reported the above. Not bad! Success with this strategy also hinges on promotion. It's not enough to simply flip the pricing switch. There's simply too much out there now. So, get the word out and make that your priority. Leading technology sites like AppAdvice and Indie App Santa are ideal for this type of promotion, as well as relevant communities on Reddit (for example, the iOS apps subreddit). Remember, when offering an in-app purchase for free, ensure that it's non-consumable (think "Remove Ads" or "Unlock Premium Feature") so you preserve the value proposition and secure a lasting conversion once users experience the upgrade. 2. Mastering App Store Optimization (ASO) App Store Optimization, or ASO, is often referred to as SEO for the App Store, and it plays a crucial role in organic discovery. At its core, ASO is about ensuring your app stands out in a crowded marketplace by optimizing key elements of your app's store listing. This includes your app title, description, keywords, and even the icon and screenshots. It's a constantly evolving art, but it pays dividends once it's implemented correctly. Many critics argue that ASO isn't as effective as it once was. In truth, ASO continues to work — but only when your app delivers genuine value. ASO for a bad app won't matter. A great app with no ASO may not hit. You want both — an app genuinely solving a problem paired with effective ASO can equal an attractive business. Big brands, such as Uber or Kindle, have large marketing budgets and strong brand recognition that allow them to leverage ASO successfully. These companies invest in high-quality content and consistently update their listings to resonate with potential users. For smaller developers, though, the lesson is the same: a good ASO strategy can boost your organic downloads, but again — it requires an app that meets or exceeds user expectations. While ASO can be a massive topic to dive into, simply focus on the fundamentals first. Ensure your app's title is both catchy and descriptive, use a set of well-researched keywords, and back it all up with a strong user experience. In the past, I've even experimented with techniques like leveraging app store reviews to ramp up specific keyword rankings. I've found that strategy to be effective, and it continues to deliver results even today. The bottom line is that when executed correctly, ASO lays a solid foundation for your app's long-term visibility and success. Don't skip it! 3. Embracing localization for global reach Localization goes far beyond simply translating your app's language. It's about tailoring your app's entire presentation to speak directly to users in different regions. By localizing your app name, keywords, and (if possible) screenshots and descriptions, you can tap into markets that might be overlooked when you limit your content to English. Start small here, as with ASO. Try focusing on the most visible elements — things like your app's name and the keywords associated with it. For instance, subtle differences such as using "localised" instead of "localized" can make a significant impact in certain markets like the UK. Once you see an uptick in regional downloads, consider gradually localizing additional assets like screenshots and in-app descriptions. This incremental approach helps manage costs while measuring impact, ensuring that each step in localization is justified by increased user engagement. One minor downside of partial localization is that users in non-English speaking markets might find the in-app content still in English. However, the benefits of reaching a larger audience typically outweigh that. By adjusting your app's metadata for different regions, you offer a more personalized experience that can dramatically boost downloads in countries that would have otherwise been difficult to crack. 4. Leveraging exclusive PR opportunities Public relations still holds significant power in the digital age, especially when it comes to launching an app. Instead of spreading your story to multiple outlets, consider granting an exclusive to a single, respected publication. Pitching your launch as an exclusive story can help you secure quality coverage from top-tier media outlets like TechCrunch or VentureBeat, where it might be otherwise harder to gain attention. Here's how it works: Identify the right reporter or editor within the target publication. Tailor a pitch that not only explains your app's unique value, but also offers them the first look at your launch. Offer them exclusive rights to your story. Now, you're effectively flattering their credibility — and many publications appreciate that. This approach creates a sense of urgency and pride, which can lead to some favorable coverage. That said, there is a trade-off, though. By pitching an exclusive, you're limiting your audience to that one publication for the time being. If the pitch doesn't land, you may not have immediate alternatives. In one case, I pitched an exclusive to a well-known outlet only to receive a delayed response stating that the story had already been published elsewhere. Despite this small risk, the rewards are worth it when the exclusive generates buzz and positions your app as a must-watch launch. The key is to get in front of the media early in your launch cycle, securing the attention you need before your app goes live. 5. Cracking the App Store feature hack Finally, one of the most enticing strategies for app developers is the App Store feature hack. Securing a spot on the featured section in the App Store can lead to a massive influx of downloads. But, how do you get your app noticed by the right people at Apple? It starts with doing your homework. Every category in the App Store is carefully managed by a dedicated team. Use LinkedIn to identify the right App Store manager for your app's category and tools like Email Hunter to locate their email address quickly. Then, craft a compelling pitch explaining why your app deserves a feature placement. Timing is crucial here. Rather than pitching before your app is approved, wait until it has successfully passed review. This extra layer of credibility enhances your pitch and increases your chances of receiving a favorable response. You can even do this right within App Store Connect now (look at the sidebar under "Featuring" → "Nominations"). When reaching out, give them plenty of notice — ideally at least two to three weeks before your launch date. For certain categories, like gaming, there might even be a preference for specific launch days (one manager noted that Thursday is often ideal). While this method might take extra effort, landing a featured spot can exponentially increase your app's visibility, driving both organic downloads and long-term engagement. Wrapping up Growing an app successfully requires a multi-faceted approach rather than a single formula. All of these strategies play a crucial role in increasing downloads and engagement. To recap: A well-executed apps-gone-free campaign can drive an immediate surge in users. ASO ensures long-term visibility. Localization helps tap into new markets. Exclusive PR generates media buzz. Securing an App Store feature can provide a massive boost in organic downloads. As always, the key to success lies in the long term execution. These techniques have been proven across industries, but their effectiveness depends on delivering real value to users — and that's something only you can control. By integrating and testing different growth tactics, you can build a sustainable framework for app success. Every app is unique! So experiment, track results, and iterate to find what works best. With persistence and smart execution, your app can definitely stand out in today's crowded marketplace.

CRMs enhance campaign outreach by centralizing and analyzing vast amounts of voter data, allowing targeted communication strategies. They enable campaigns to segment voters based on demographics or past voting behavior, creating tailored messaging that resonates more effectively with different audiences. CRMs can automate the delivery of these messages across multiple platforms, ensuring that outreach is consistent and timely. This targeted approach not only improves engagement rates but also helps campaigns strategically allocate resources toward the most promising voter segments. Why are CRMs better than spreadsheets for political campaigns? CRMs excel over spreadsheets by providing a dynamic, interconnected environment where all campaign data is automatically updated and accessible. Unlike static spreadsheets that can become outdated or contain fragmented information, CRMs centralize data management, preventing data silos. They offer automation features for routine tasks, such as communication scheduling and data entry, which reduces the likelihood of human error and frees up staff for strategic tasks. CRMs also provide analytical tools for data-driven decision-making, whereas spreadsheets require more manual manipulation to generate insights. What features should I prioritize in a political CRM? When evaluating a political CRM, prioritize features that support voter data management, targeted outreach, compliance tracking, and fundraising. Essential tools include voter segmentation for personalized communications, robust analytics to track campaign progress, and automation capabilities to streamline repetitive processes. Furthermore, ensure the CRM offers secure data storage and management to protect sensitive information. Look for flexibility in integration with other platforms to create a smooth workflow that aligns with your campaign's specific operational needs. How can Miniloop specifically reduce my campaign's CRM costs? Miniloop can significantly cut CRM operating costs by eliminating the common expense of per-seat licensing fees, allowing campaigns to only pay for the features they actively use. This cost-effective approach is particularly beneficial for campaigns with diverse teams where user counts can fluctuate. By providing a custom-built CRM to match the campaign's unique processes, Miniloop reduces the need for additional software adjustments or workarounds often associated with generic CRM options. This tailored fit means better resource allocation and fewer inefficiencies, ultimately streamlining both budgeting and operations.

title: HPE: Designing Data Centers for AI at Scale
summary: One of the biggest inefficiencies in modern data centers is the disconnect between IT systems and the physical facility. Servers, storage, and networking are often managed separately from cooling, power, and space planning. As a result, many data cen...
body_text: HPE: Designing Data Centers for AI at Scale 30 Jul 2026 • 2 minute read One of the biggest inefficiencies in modern data centers is the disconnect between IT systems and the physical facility. Servers, storage, and networking are often managed separately from cooling, power, and space planning. As a result, many data centers operate at just 30-40% of their actual IT capacity, despite being designed for much more. HPE’s approach is centered on bridging this gap through a unified, end-to-end view of data center operations. Using the Cadence Reality Digital Twin Platform , HPE can model both IT infrastructure and facility systems within a single environment. This enables teams to understand how changes on one side, such as adding new AI hardware, impact the entire system in real time. This capability is especially important as AI infrastructure continues to evolve rapidly. With shorter hardware refresh cycles and increasing reliance on GPUs, data centers need to be more flexible and adaptable than ever. Cadence’s modeling provides HPE with detailed representations of components, including advanced systems such as liquid-cooled hardware, enabling more accurate planning and integration. HPE has already put this into practice by implementing a digital twin in its Geneva data center, using it as a live demonstration of how simulation-driven design and operations can improve efficiency. Today, this approach has expanded across HPE’s AI-focused deployment, becoming a standard part of how new data centers are designed and managed. The benefits extend beyond design, though. During operations, the Cadence Reality Digital Twin Platform provides an environment for testing scenarios, optimizing performance, and improving energy efficiency, all without disrupting live systems. By combining HPE’s infrastructure expertise with Cadence’s modeling capabilities, the result is a smarter and more responsive data center that’s built for the demands of today and the rapid changes of tomorrow. Learn more about how HPE is bridging the gap between IT and data centers . “Designed with Cadence” is a series of videos that showcases creative products and technologies that are accelerating industry innovation using Cadence tools and solutions. For more Designed with Cadence videos, check out the Cadence website and YouTube channel .

title: How Much Does a Performance Bond Cost
summary: Explore factors influencing performance bond costs in construction projects. Learn how financial history and project specifics affect pricing.
body_text: What is the cost of a performance bond? The construction performance bond cost can vary widely depending on several factors, including the size and type of project, the contractor's financial history, bonding capacity, and creditworthiness, the duration of the bond, and the specific b set by the obligee (the party requiring the bond). Generally, performance bond costs are calculated with bond rates, typically ranging from 1% to 5%. There is the general formula you can apply to determine the surety bond costs: Price you pay = Contract Price * Premium Rate For example, if the contract price is $1,000,000 and the performance bond rate of 5%, the cost of the performance bond would be $50,000. However, rates can be higher or lower based on the aforementioned factors. Additionally, some surety bond companies may charge additional fees or require collateral depending on the risk associated with the project and the contractor. Find out more about how much performance bonds cost . Bond Amount - Bond Cost $5,000 $50 - $150 $10,000 $100 - $300 $20,000 $200 - $600 $50,000 $500 - $1500 $100,000 $1000 - $3000 $200,000 $2000 - $6000 Detailed Examples of Premiums and Rates Here are some examples of calculations based on different scenarios and pricing structures: Example One: A performance bond for a construction company working on a project to construct a major expansion to the local public university campus is projected to cost $1,500,000. Their surety provider offers them a flat rate of $15 per $1,000, and thus they will be obligated to pay $22,500 in premium costs. Example Two: A contractor takes a payment bond for a new construction project also worth $1,500,000. The surety party offers them a tiered rate for their premiums, calculated as the sum of 5% the first $500,000, 3% of the second $500,000, and 2% of the remaining $500,000. In this way, the total cost of the contractor’s premiums will be calculated as: ($500,000 * 5% = $25,000) ($500,000 * 3% = $15,000 ) ($500,000 * 2% = $10,000) = $50,000 . Terms To Know About in Performance Bond Rates When calculating premiums and rates for performance/payment bonds, there are a few key terms that are important to understand: Flat rate: The price of a flat rate premium does not change based on the value of the contract; it will remain at a fixed value. Dollar Rate per Thousand ($/M): The price is calculated based on a fixed rate per $1,000 of the total contract value, meaning that larger contracts will have a proportionally larger premium. So, for example, a contract for a large construction project on a skyscraper valued at a $1,000,000 will have a premium 100 times greater than a smaller maintenance project with a contract worth $10,000. This often referred to as $/M, with M representing $1,000. Tiered rate: For a tiered rate structure, while the premium is calculated as a percentage of the total value of the original contract, the percentage gradually decreases as the value of the contract increases. So, for instance, a large construction project worth $3,000,000 might have premiums worth 5% of their contract for the first $1,000,000, 3% of the contract for the next $1,000,000, and only 1.5% of the remaining $1,000,000. Change Order (CO): A change order is any change in the value of the original project contract after it has been initiated, which then affects the premium values and the overall cost of the bond. Additional Premium(AP)/Overrun: A type of change order that increases the original contract amount and the associated premiums. Return Premium(RP): A type of change order that decreases the original contract amount and the associated premiums. Factors That Determine the Performance Bond Premium There are two factors that drive 80% of a performance bond premium. 1. Personal Credit Score When a contractor or business applies for a performance bond, the surety company issuing the bond will assess the financial stability and personal credit score of the applicant. This assessment helps the surety company determine the level of risk involved in providing the bond. The cost of performance bonds can vary based on the applicant's creditworthiness. Contractors with higher credit scores might qualify for lower premium rates because they are perceived as lower-risk clients. 2. Financial History A contractor's financial history can influence a performance bond's cost. When a surety company evaluates a contractor's financial history, they assess the contractor's ability to fulfill their contractual obligations and complete the project. Much like the personal credit score, the financial performance of a contractor allows the surety to assess your company's risk. Sureties usually look at your financial statements, working capital, track record, industry reputation, and other factors. If you are deemed high risk, your bond cost will be higher than if you are deemed low risk. Other Factors There are other factors that have less of an impact. Contract Price, duration and size of project, public or private sector, government requirement. Contract Size and Scope : Larger, more complex projects involve greater financial risk , resulting in higher premiums . ‍ Location and Jurisdiction : Different states and localities have unique bonding requirements . Some require full contract coverage , while others only mandate partial coverage . ‍ Surety Provider Policies : Each surety company has different risk assessment models , leading to varying premium rates . ‍ Contractor’s Past Performance : A strong history of successful projects may qualify a contractor for lower premium rates . ‍ Miscellaneous Fees : Additional charges include change order fees, maintenance fees, and time completion surcharges . Do you need to pay to renew your performance bond? Whether or not you need to renew a performance bond yearly depends on the specific terms and duration of the bond, as well as the requirements set forth by the obligee (the party requiring the bond). Here are some common scenarios: Single Project Bonds : Performance bonds are often issued for individual construction projects. Once the project is completed and all obligations are fulfilled, the bond may expire automatically. In this case, there's typically no need for renewal unless the project extends beyond the initial bond term. Continuous Bonds : Some performance bonds are issued on a continuous basis, covering multiple projects or a specific period, such as a year. In these cases, the bond may need to be renewed annually or at specified intervals to maintain coverage. Renewal Requirements : Even for single project bonds, there may be situations where renewal is necessary. For example, if the project timeline extends beyond the initial bond term, you may need to renew the bond to ensure coverage until project completion. Additionally, if there are changes to the project scope, terms of the contract, or bonding requirements, renewal may be required to reflect these changes. Obligee Requirements : The obligee may specify renewal requirements in the contract documents or bonding agreement. It's essential to review these requirements carefully and ensure compliance to avoid any lapse in coverage. Surety Company Policies : The policies of the surety company that issued the bond may also dictate renewal procedures and requirements. They may offer options for automatic renewal or require you to initiate the renewal process by submitting a renewal application and paying the premium. Role of Surety Company The surety company plays a crucial role in the process of the bonding process. They have several essential responsibilities as they issue the construction bond. Bond Underwriting : The surety company assesses the risk associated with issuing the bond, i.e. does the contractor have the financial and performance capability to complete the project. Based on this assessment, the surety determines whether to issue the bond and, if so, under what bond terms and conditions. Bond Limitations and Conditions : The surety company may impose certain limitations or bond terms, such as maximum payout amounts, duration of coverage, or specific requirements for claims handling. The contractor must adhere to these terms to maintain the validity of the bond. Bond Issuance : The bonding company provides the necessary documentation to the contractor. This includes the construction performance bond cost and the bond itself, which serves as a guarantee to the project owner (obligee) that the contractor will fulfill their obligations according to the bond terms of the contract. Bonding Services : Throughout the duration of the project, the surety company may provide support and guidance to the contractor. This could include assistance with bond-related paperwork, advice on risk management, or guidance on how to avoid potential claims and bond penalties. Claims Handling : If a claim is filed against the bond due to the contractor's failure to perform according to the contract terms, the surety company investigates the claim and determines its validity. If the claim is found to be legitimate, the surety may fulfill its obligation by compensating the obligee for the losses incurred. Overall, the surety company acts as a financial guarantor, providing assurance to project owners that the contractor will fulfill their contractual obligations. Their involvement helps facilitate trust and confidence in the construction industry and ensures that projects are completed successfully. How does the surety company collect payment after settling a claim? When surety companies settles a claim on a performance bond, the surety companies would pay for the contractor first. However, they would need to collect payment as the contractor violates the bond terms and conditions. To recover the paid out bond coverage, the surety companies usually pursue contractor through legal means to collect the fund. Specifically, before issuing a performance bond, the surety company often requires the principal to sign an indemnification agreement . This agreement is a contract that stipulates the principal to be responsible for reimbursing the bonding agency for any losses incurred due to a claim on the bond. With the indemnification agreement, the surety bond companies can then pursue the principal for repayment according to the terms of the agreement legally. In some cases, the surety bond companies may require the principal to provide bond collateral upfront as security for the surety company against potential claims. If a claim is settled, the surety may retain or liquidate the collateral to cover the costs. If a claim is not, the surety would return the bond collateral to the contractor. Subrogation is the legal process by which the surety assumes the rights of the obligee (the party who filed the claim) to pursue recovery from any third parties responsible for the losses. If another party, such as a subcontractor, contributed to the failure that led to the claim, the surety may pursue them for reimbursement. If the principal refuses or is unable to repay the surety for the settled claim, the surety may take legal action to enforce the indemnification agreement or recover the funds through other legal means. Overall, the surety company employs various strategies to recover the amount paid out on a settled claim, aiming to minimize its losses and maintain its financial stability. What is a performance bond? In the construction context, a construction performance bond protects against the risk of a contractor not completing the project as agreed. Performance bonds are typically required on larger construction projects, government contracts, and projects with high financial stakes. They provide performance guarantees and financial guarantees for property owners, contractors, and the public, helping mitigate the risks associated with non-performance or delays of private or public projects. The Federal Miller Act mandates the use of contract surety bonds, which include payment bond and bid bond in addition to performance surety bond, for all public construction projects exceeding $100,000. Some local legislation mandate construction bonds and contract bonds for projects with lower value. As time progresses, many private project owners realize the advantages of contract bond, leading to more application of these financial insurance policy. Specifically, performance bond is the most relevant to the protection of project owners as well as public safety. Suppose the contractor fails to meet their contractual obligations, such as finishing the project on time, within budget, or meeting quality standards. In that case, the project owner can make a claim against the performance bond. If the claim is valid, the surety bond company that issued the bond will compensate the project owner up to the bond amount. This compensation can cover the costs of completing the project or rectifying any deficiencies caused by the contractor's failure to perform. This article focuses on performance bonds, including what they are, why you need them, and how to get a contract surety bond and a performance bond claim. Performance Bond vs Other Contractor Bond It's important to note that a performance bond is distinct from payment bonds and bid bonds. While a performance bond focuses on the performance guarantee of the project, a payment bond ensures that the contractor pays their subcontractors, suppliers, and laborers as required by the contract and a bid bond guarantees compensation to the bond owner if the bidder fails to begin a project. The terms and conditions of performance bonds can vary, and they are typically regulated by laws and regulations specific to each country or jurisdiction. Conclusion The cost of a surety bond is relatively simply in the process of bond application. However, upon issuance and bond approval, there are additional areas of payment possible for the performance guarantee of a construction project. Specifically, contractors may need to pay for bond renewal and for claim reimbursement. Overall, the bond coverage relates to contract value and applicants' financial status.

title: Website marketing: A guide for the AI search era
summary: Website marketing strategies that build the credibility AI systems use to decide which brands to recommend.
body_text: For years, website marketing meant search visibility: ranking for the right queries and earning the click. The way people search has changed. They still use Google, but they also ask AI tools for direct answers. These tools draw on training data and the sources they retrieve to decide which brands are credible enough to surface or cite. That shifts the goal from visibility to credibility: proof that your brand is trustworthy enough to be recommended. The techniques are largely the same. What they’re accomplishing is different. In this guide, we’ll cover 12 website marketing techniques that now build credibility across search, AI tools, and the channels your audience uses. What is website marketing? Website marketing is the process of promoting your website so people who need your product, service, or expertise can find your business, learn from your content, and become customers. Today, that also means managing how your brand appears across the channels and sources people and AI tools use to evaluate it. The four layers of website marketing A strategic website marketing plan is what moves your brand from competing for attention to earning a position as a trusted destination. It builds the signals that determine where your brand shows up, how AI tools understand it, and whether they recommend it. Those signals work across four layers, each a prerequisite for the next: Discoverability: Can AI tools find you? Your content needs to be easy for search engines and AI tools to find and access. This is the foundation everything else builds on. Clarity: Can AI tools understand you? Once found, AI needs to understand what your brand does and who it serves. The messaging across your site and external sources like reviews and directories needs to be consistent, so AI shows you to the people most likely to need what you offer. Authority: Do credible sources validate you? Your brand needs evidence that it is a credible entity in its category. Coverage from reputable publications and third-party mentions both strengthen authority. Trust: Would AI tools recommend you? Your brand needs signals that it delivers on what it claims. Positive reviews and confirmation from independent sources are what give buyers and AI tools the confidence to act. Why website marketing is more critical now than ever Our research suggests AI search will start driving more visitors to websites than traditional search by 2028. And the average AI search visitor is worth 4.4 times more than a traditional organic visitor, from a conversion standpoint, which makes AI visibility a revenue issue, not just a traffic one. Every 100 visitors your brand earns from AI search carries the conversion value of 440 traditional organic visitors. Roughly 60% of searches on traditional search engines now end without a click , so ranking alone no longer guarantees a visit. 12 techniques to use in your website marketing strategy In keyword-based search, each marketing tactic had a clear role: rank, reach, convert, or retain. In AI search, those roles overlap. A review builds trust, a comparison page shapes an AI answer, a guest post strengthens authority, and a social profile confirms your brand is active and relevant. The 12 techniques below show how familiar tactics work together when credibility is the goal. 1. Search engine optimization: Build the discoverability layer search engines and AI tools depend on Search engine optimization (SEO) is the process of improving your website so it can appear in search results when people look for what you offer. In an AI search environment, SEO is still the foundation. It makes your important pages easier for search engines to find, read, rank, and connect to relevant queries. Start with the pages that matter most to your business. These are usually your homepage, product or service pages, and pages that already bring traffic or leads. Use Semrush's Keyword Magic Tool to check the search volume, difficulty, and intent for a few terms related to the page. Then pick the term that best matches what people search for and what the page actually offers. For example, an accounting software page might target "accounting software for small businesses" or "best accounting software." If your site is new, start with your homepage and core product or service pages. Make sure each page clearly explains what you offer, who it is for, and what action visitors should take next. If your site already gets search traffic, Semrush's Organic Rankings tool can show which keywords you already rank for. Next, use Google Search Console's (GSC) free Page Indexing report to check whether your important pages are indexed. This shows which pages Google can find and include in search results. Then improve each page: Match the page to the search term : A page targeting "best accounting software" should compare the options and explain which type of business each one suits Cover the on-page basics : a clear SEO title, proper heading structure (H1, then H2s and H3s), internal links from related pages, and fast, mobile-friendly loading. Our guide to promoting your website walks through each. Check progress : Use Semrush's Position Tracking to monitor rankings across Google and AI tools, and revisit the title, headings, and content match if a page stalls. 2. Content marketing: Create the evidence buyers and AI systems look for Content marketing is the practice of creating useful content, like blogs, guides, comparisons, and how-to articles, that answers questions your audience is already searching for. Content marketing gives search engines, AI tools, and buyers something useful to evaluate. To put this into practice: Find real questions your audience asks: Use Semrush's Keyword Strategy Builder to enter one topic related to your business and add three to five related keywords. The tool groups related questions and subtopics into a content plan. Choose the most relevant questions: Pick two or three questions that closely relate to your product, service, or expertise. Find the content gap: Search each question on Google and review the top three results. Look for what is missing, outdated, too generic, or not useful enough. Create one focused page that fills the gap: Include specific examples, data, screenshots, customer insights, or expert input where relevant. Articles that compare options, show examples, and answer follow-up questions give readers enough detail to decide and give AI tools something worth citing. Zapier is a strong example. Its guides cover side-by-side software comparisons and detailed workflow walkthroughs, making its educational resources some of its highest-traffic pages. The same specificity that earns these pages organic traffic also makes them useful sources when AI tools summarize topics or compare options. Semrush's Top Pages report shows how any domain's pages perform across organic search, AI Overviews, AI mode, and AI tools. Each page shows traffic, keyword count, referring domains, and LLM prompt volume. Run it on a competitor's domain to find which pages appear in multiple channels and which topics are worth replicating. According to Semrush’s AI Visibility Overview , Zapier earns roughly 69,000 mentions* and about 128,000 citations** across major AI platforms, spread across more than 47,000 different pages. 3. AI SEO: Optimize for AI recommendations, not just rankings AI SEO (also called generative engine optimization, or GEO) is the process of improving how your brand appears in AI-generated answers. SEO focuses on pages, rankings, and how you appear in search results. AI SEO focuses on prompts, mentions, citations, competitors, and how AI tools describe your brand. Start by checking the questions your buyers are likely to ask AI tools. For example: "What is the best invoicing software for small businesses?" "What are the top alternatives to [competitor]?" "Which tools are best for automating invoices?" Look at whether your brand appears, how it is described, which competitors appear with it, and which sources the AI tool cites. To improve your AI visibility: Give AI tools brand context: Comparison pages, FAQs, and guides give AI tools the detail they need to describe your brand accurately. Back claims with proof: Specific examples, data, and customer stories make your claims easier to verify and trust. Make your brand information consistent: Keep your product description, audience, use cases, pricing, and positioning consistent across your website, profiles, reviews, and third-party mentions. Build outside authority: Reviews, mentions, and press coverage show AI tools that other sources vouch for your brand. Update pages AI tools already cite: Keep your content accurate, current, and useful so AI tools have better information to reference. Checking a few prompts manually is a good starting point. With Semrush’s AI Visibility Toolkit , you can monitor these signals across major AI platforms at scale. Use the “Narrative Drivers” dashboard to track share of voice, mentions, and competitor visibility. The “Perception” dashboard shows how AI systems describe your brand and highlights opportunities to improve sentiment. And the “Questions” dashboard reveals the prompts users ask AI tools, helping you identify content opportunities and refine your positioning. Further reading: How to Rank in AI Search 4. User experience (UX): Convert the traffic your marketing earns UX is the practice of designing your website so visitors can quickly understand what you offer, trust what they see, and know what to do next. To improve UX: Make the page promise clear: The headline should answer "what is this, and who is it for?" within a few seconds. Focus on your highest-impact pages first: Start with your homepage, main product or service pages, and checkout, signup, or demo page. These are usually the pages most closely tied to traffic, leads, or sales. Make navigation easy to follow: Keep the menu simple, visible, and consistent. If visitors regularly rely on the browser's back button just to get around your own site, that's a sign navigation needs fixing. Show the next step early: Place the main call-to-action (CTA) near the top of the page. Use short, actionable steps like "Book a demo," "See pricing," "Start free trial," or "Download the guide." Remove competing actions: Give the page one primary CTA tied to your main goal. Secondary links are fine as long as the primary action is the one that stands out visually. Add proof near the promise: Place reviews, customer logos, testimonials, case study results, or security badges close to the CTA. Make the page easy to scan: Use short sections, clear headings, bullets, visuals, and white space so visitors can find answers quickly. Keep the design clean and consistent: Use the same fonts, colors, and styling across every page. Answer common objections directly on the page: Address price, setup, timing, cancellation, support, or risk in a short line or FAQ on the page itself. Secure your site with SSL: Your site address should start with "https." Ask your hosting provider for an "SSL certificate" if your site doesn't have one. Check mobile usability: Open the page on your phone. If you have to pinch to zoom or buttons are too small to tap, your website platform's mobile settings need adjusting. Diagnose and fix page speed: Use a tool like PageSpeed Insights or Semrush Site Audit to check whether slow load times are causing visitors to leave, then fix whatever it flags as the biggest issue. 5. Search ads: Buy visibility while your organic authority builds Search ads are paid placements that can appear when people search for terms related to what you sell. Many search campaigns use a pay-per-click (PPC) model, where you're charged when someone clicks your ad. Use paid search ads when you want to reach people who are already showing buying intent. For example, "black linen shirts for men" shows stronger intent than "is linen good for summer." Google now places ads in and around AI Overviews . This keeps your brand visible even as the results page changes. To run better search ads: Choose high-intent search terms : Start with terms people use when they're close to buying, booking, signing up, or requesting a quote, like "buy," "pricing," or "near me." Check cost and competition : Before setting a budget, check cost-per-click (CPC) and competitive density (how many other advertisers are bidding on the same term) in a tool like Semrush’s Keyword Overview. Start small, and increase spend once you see what's working. Match the ad to the search : If someone searches "best project management tool for small business," your ad's headline and description should include that same phrase, not a generic line like "Try our software today." Send clicks to the right page : A pricing search should go to a pricing or product page, not a general blog post. Track business outcomes : Set up conversion tracking in Google Ads to measure leads, signups, purchases, demo requests, or quote requests. Move budget toward what converts : Using what you tracked above, increase spend on terms that bring signups or purchases, and pause the ones that get clicks without any of those outcomes. Search ads help you capture high-intent demand now while your organic authority grows over time. 6. Organic social media: Signal brand presence across every platform AI can validate Organic social media means publishing posts and engaging with people on social platforms to build presence and community. Social media is one of the clearest two-way channels in marketing. Customers reply, ask questions, share opinions, and interact with each other. Consistency across platforms also matters for credibility: it is one of the signals buyers and AI tools use to confirm a brand is active and real. To build a stronger organic social presence: Start with one or two platforms: Choose platforms where your audience already talks about your topic. For B2B brands, prioritize LinkedIn, YouTube, and X. For B2C brands, Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, and Pinterest make more sense. Make your profiles clear: Explain what your business does, who it serves, and where people should go next. Publish content people can use: Share tips, product use cases, customer stories, short videos, and answers to common questions. Invite people to respond: Ask questions, run polls, reply to comments, and respond to direct messages. Public replies show other people that your brand is active and listening. Encourage customer content: Reshare customer posts, testimonials, reviews, or product examples with permission. Track what resonates: Look at comments, shares, saves, clicks, profile visits, and direct messages. These signals show stronger interest than likes alone. Duolingo is a strong example of organic social media in action. Its social presence turned the Duo mascot into a recognizable brand character, and its comments, replies, trends, and creator-style posts made the brand part of public conversations about language learning. That public activity gives buyers more ways to discover and evaluate the brand. Managing brand social media means juggling several jobs at once: posting, replying, monitoring mentions, and tracking performance. Semrush Social Toolkit centralizes the work: Social Poster schedules your posts Social Content AI drafts ideas and captions when you need to publish regularly Media Monitoring finds customer content and brand mentions across social platforms, blogs, forums, and news Social Content Insights shows which of your posts are actually earning comments, shares, saves, clicks, and profile visits Further reading: How social media SEO can boost your visibility 7. Social media advertising: Amplify reach across the channels your audience uses Social media advertising means paying to promote your brand, content, or offer on social platforms like LinkedIn, Meta, TikTok, YouTube, X, or Pinterest, either through a platform's ad system or by partnering with a creator who already has an engaged audience. Social ads are useful when you want to build awareness, test a new angle, promote an offer, reach people who've already shown interest, or send targeted visitors to your website. To run social ads well: Start with something worth amplifying: Choose a post that is performing well and boost it with paid amplification. Use Semrush's Social Content Insights to see which of your existing posts are already earning engagement. Choose one audience for one reason: Target new buyers by interest or demographic, or target people who've already shown interest, like past website visitors or video viewers. Match the page to the ad: Send people to the page that matches the ad’s offering. For example, if the ad's headline promises a discount, that discount should be visible on the page without scrolling. Test one variable per test: Test one message, audience, format, or offer at a time. If you change all of them at once, you will not know what caused the result. Measure based on the campaign goal: For awareness, look at reach, video views, profile visits, or site visits. For traffic, look at clicks and landing page engagement. For leads or sales, look at signups, purchases, demo requests, and how much you're spending for each conversion. Scale only after the signal is clear: Set a target cost per result before launching, for example, $50 per signup. Once your actual cost is consistently at or below that number, increase the budget. If it's higher, change the message, audience, or page first. If you are using creators, choose partners based on audience fit, engagement, and content quality. Ask for a genuine comparison, walkthrough, or product experience rather than a scripted ad read. Useful creator content earns more trust from the audience. Semrush's Influencer Analytics lets you search creators across YouTube, Twitch, Instagram, and TikTok by topic. You can also see their audience's demographics, how well a sponsored post from them is likely to perform, and which other brands they've worked with before. 8. Email marketing: Own the audience no algorithm can take away Email marketing is sending emails to people who have signed up to hear from your business. These include newsletters, product updates, offers, event invites, educational content, or abandoned cart reminders. Your email list is one of the few marketing assets you fully own. Email marketing gives you a direct way to reach people who've already shown interest in your brand. To get started: Set up an email marketing platform first: Use tools like Mailchimp, Klaviyo, or Kit to collect email addresses, send emails to your list, and see how each email performs. Place signup forms on the pages people already visit: Your homepage or checkout page, with an offer like a discount or downloadable asset. Set up a welcome email campaign: The moment someone subscribes, send an automated welcome email. Segment your audience: Group subscribers by interest, behavior, or stage, like new subscribers, free trial users, and repeat customers. Create a different campaign for each segment: Give each segment its own message and a relevant call to action (CTA). A new subscriber gets an introduction to your product, while a repeat customer might get an offer to buy again. A/B test your emails: Create two versions of the same email with only one thing changed, like the subject line, and use the metrics in the next step to see which one performs better. Track open rate (how many people open the email) and click-through rate (how many click a link inside it) , but judge real success by signups, purchases, and return visits. Maintain your list: Remove inactive subscribers and incorrect email addresses. 9. Affiliate marketing: Turn independent endorsements into authority signals Affiliate marketing is a marketing practice where creators, publishers, or industry websites recommend your product to their audience, in exchange for a commission on each sale. When a publisher who already covers your category recommends your product, that third-party mention is a signal search engines use to confirm your brand is a credible option in that space. To find and work with affiliates: Sign up for an affiliate network: Platforms like ShareASale, Impact, or Awin create your tracked referral link and pay commissions automatically. Search for sites that already review your category: Search "[competitor] alternatives" or "[your category] review" and see which publications come up repeatedly. Those are your realistic candidates. Check each candidate's content: Read two or three recent posts to confirm they genuinely review products like yours and get real engagement, comments and shares. Give partners real material: Provide a free account or sample, plus the problem it solves, who it's for, and pricing, so they can write a genuine review. Track who actually converts: Use your network's dashboard to see which partners send paying customers. Offer your best performers a higher commission, or ask for a deeper piece, like a full comparison. Here's what this looks like in practice: Exit Five, a B2B marketing publication, featured Knak in one of their newsletters. Since Exit Five's audience is interested in B2B marketing, the recommendation reached people actively looking for relevant tools. When a reader clicks the link and buys, Knak pays Exit Five a commission based on the revenue generated. A genuine recommendation from a publication your buyers already trust builds real authority for your brand. 10. Online reviews: Build the trust signals AI and buyers both weigh Online reviews are public feedback your customers leave about their experience, on platforms like Google, Yelp, G2, or Trustpilot. Reviews show what customers actually think about your brand, their experience, and the quality of what you offer. That public opinion helps both people and AI tools understand your brand from a customer's perspective. To strengthen your review profile: Ask right after a good experience: The best time to ask for a review is while it's still recent. Keep new reviews coming in steadily: Recent reviews give buyers and third-party platforms fresher reputation signals. Watch every platform: A bad pattern on a site you're ignoring can damage your reputation. Respond to every review, good or bad: A thoughtful response shows future customers, and search engines, that you're paying attention to your customers’ experiences with the brand. With Semrush's Review Management , you can handle your online brand reputation from a single dashboard: Send automatic SMS or email review requests right after a purchase or service Pull reviews from dozens of platforms into a single view Draft AI-generated responses to reviews, edit them, and post directly from the dashboard Benchmark your review count and rating directly against named competitors through Review Analytics Further reading: How to Build and Manage Your Online Reputation 11. Guest blogging: Expand your brand's citation footprint Guest blogging means writing articles for credible websites, like industry blogs, trade publications, or newsletters, to reach audiences beyond your own. Each credible site that publishes your work becomes another place where your expertise is documented and linked back to you. That external coverage builds your brand authority. For example, Tomoko Yokoi's author bio on Forbes links directly to her own website and her book's listing on Amazon, turning one guest article into two credible references back to her work. To get started with guest posting : Find sites that already write about your topic. Search for "[your topic] blog," or check where competitors have published guest articles. Check the site's authority before pitching. Run the domain through Semrush's free Backlink Checker tool and look at its Authority Score, a 0-100 rating of how strong the site's backlink profile is. Make sure your author bio links back to your site or work, the way Tomoko Yokoi's bio does. A linked author bio strengthens the connection between the guest post and your brand. 12. Digital PR: Earn mentions beyond your own website Digital PR is the process of earning online coverage for your brand through media mentions, expert quotes, interviews, data stories, reports, podcasts, newsletters, and industry publications. When credible publications mention your brand, product, data, or expertise, they create third-party proof that buyers, search engines, and AI tools can use to understand your authority. To get the most out of digital PR: Start with a real story: Pitch something worth covering: original data, a trend, expert commentary, a product launch, a case study, or a strong industry point of view. Choose outlets buyers and AI tools trust: Look for publications your audience already reads and outlets AI tools often cite for your topic/industry. Build a focused media list: Find journalists who have recently covered topics in your industry. Recent, relevant coverage is a strong sign your pitch may fit their beat. Build the pitch around their work: Reference their recent coverage and explain why your story fits. Give them a clear angle, a short summary, an expert quote, and any useful data. Track outreach and act on what it tells you: If a pitch goes unanswered after about a week, follow up once. If one story angle gets picked up, use that pattern in future pitches. PR mentions are credible third-party references that can support your brand’s visibility across search results, AI answers, and buyer research. Here’s how you can use Semrush’s AI PR Toolkit to streamline your PR outreach: In Semrush's AI-Cited Media tool, enter your topic, language, and country to see outlets ranked by AI Trust score, a 1-100 rating of how likely each one is to be cited when AI tools answer questions on it. Select a handful of outlets from the "Most influential outlets" list, then check the Collective AI Media Impact panel on the right. It tells you whether your picks are an optimal mix, marked High impact. Once you've picked your outlets, click "View contributing journalists" to pull writers at those exact outlets straight from the Media Database , each with their industry relevance and recent article. Next, draft your email or press release with AI assistance, using your key points as the starting point. Send it from your authenticated domain or connected inbox. After outreach, use Media Monitoring to track mentions of your brand, product, report, or target keywords. Add filters to keep results relevant, and set up alerts for new mentions. You can also add website URLs to make linked mentions easier to spot later. This helps you see where your brand is being discussed, which topics are gaining coverage, and whether sentiment or mention volume is changing over time. How to choose the right tactics for your website marketing strategy Choose tactics based on which layer is your current bottleneck. Discoverability gap (your brand isn't showing up) : SEO, content marketing, search ads, social ads Clarity gap (AI tools describe your brand inaccurately or inconsistently) : AI SEO, content marketing, organic social Authority gap (credible sources aren't referencing you) : guest blogging, digital PR, affiliate marketing Trust gap (visitors aren't converting or buyers aren't confident) : reviews, UX, email marketing How to measure website marketing performance Measure website marketing performance by tracking progress across five areas: discoverability, clarity, authority, trust, and conversion. Discoverability shows whether people can find your brand. Track organic traffic, keyword rankings, referral traffic, and AI citations. Clarity shows whether AI tools and buyers understand what your brand does and who it serves. Track branded search volume, AI share of voice, and how consistently your brand is described across reviews, directories, and AI answers. Authority shows whether your brand is becoming a recognized source in your industry. Track backlinks, brand mentions, media coverage, guest posts, and third-party citations. Trust measures how people perceive your brand. Track review growth, ratings, sentiment, customer feedback, and social proof. Conversion shows whether your marketing is creating business results. Track leads, sales, demo requests, signups, assisted conversions, email subscribers, and purchases. Now that AI tools are central to how people search, improving your mentions and citations inside those tools matters. Using Semrush's AI Visibility Toolkit is a good place to start. FAQ How do I start marketing my website? To start marketing your website, identify your biggest bottleneck. If you need traffic quickly, focus on search ads and social ads. If you need long-term discoverability, prioritize SEO and content marketing. If you need more visibility in AI search, prioritize AI SEO, reviews, and third-party mentions. If visitors aren't converting, focus on UX, reviews, and social proof. If you want a channel that doesn't depend on any platform, build an email list. How do I market my website for free? To market your website for free, create useful content, optimize your most important pages for search, post on the social platforms your audience uses, collect customer reviews, and build an email list. These tactics take time, but they can bring traffic, trust, and repeat visits without paying for clicks or impressions. What is the difference between website marketing and digital marketing? The difference between website marketing and digital marketing is that website marketing focuses on attracting visitors to your website and turning them into leads, customers, subscribers, or users. Digital marketing is broader. It includes website marketing, but it can also include mobile apps, marketplaces, social platforms, paid media, email, and other online channels. How does website marketing work in the AI search era? Website marketing works in the AI search era by making your brand easier for buyers, search engines, and AI tools to find, understand, trust, and reference. People may discover your brand through Google results, AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, reviews, social posts, or third-party publications. Your website, content, reviews, and brand mentions all shape how your business appears across those touchpoints. How long does it take to see results from website marketing? It takes a few days to see results from paid website marketing channels like search ads and social ads. Organic tactics like SEO, content marketing, AI SEO, reviews, email marketing, and digital PR usually take several months to build momentum. Most businesses need a mix of faster traffic channels and slower authority-building tactics. This post was updated in 2026. Excerpts from the original article by Ana Camarena may remain.

title: Cognyte Wins ~$5 Million Agreement with New Tier-1 National Security Agency in a NATO Member Nation
summary: The agreement represents a significant new customer win in EMEA and further expands Cognyte's presence within the nation’s intelligence community.
body_text: HERZLIYA, Israel, July 14, 2026 – Cognyte Software Ltd . (NASDAQ: CGNT) (“Cognyte”), a global leader in software-driven technology for investigative analytics, today announced a ~$5 million agreement with a with a Tier-1 national security agency in a NATO member nation. The contract establishes Cognyte’s foundation with a new customer in the Europe/Middle East/Africa (EMEA) region, creating the opportunity for broader platform adoption over time. The agency selected Cognyte’s most advanced tactical SIGINT solution to support operational investigations, helping field teams enhance mission readiness, improve situational understanding and operate with greater flexibility in dynamic environments. The agreement represents a significant new customer win in EMEA and further expands Cognyte’s presence within the nation’s intelligence community. Building on successful deployments within other agencies in the country, the award reflects the operational value customers have realized from Cognyte’s platform and the trust the company has earned across the intelligence community. Security agencies worldwide are operating under pressure: threats are moving faster, data volumes are expanding and the environments in which agencies operate are growing more complex. As agencies work to protect national sovereignty against increasingly sophisticated threats, they are prioritizing investments in advanced, AI-enabled technologies that help identify, assess and mitigate risks across diverse environments. Cognyte’s investigative analytics platform, purpose built to meet these needs, delivers timely, precise and actionable intelligence that helps analysts and field teams prepare for missions, adapt to evolving situations and make informed decisions while maintaining human oversight in high-stakes environments. “For Cognyte, wins like this validate a core element of our growth strategy: proven performance with existing customers creates a natural pathway to new ones,” said Elad Sharon, Chief Executive Officer of Cognyte. “Being selected by a Tier-1 national security agency in a NATO member nation, following successful deployments with other agencies in the country, reflects the trust our platform has earned where it matters most – in operations. The demand we see in this market is durable, and we look forward to supporting the agency’s mission as its needs evolve.” About Cognyte Cognyte is a leading software-driven technology company focused on solutions for investigative analytics that enable customers to generate Actionable Intelligence for a Safer World™. Cognyte’s solutions empower law enforcement, national security and military intelligence agencies, as well as other organizations, in navigating an increasingly complex threat landscape. With offerings that leverage advanced technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI) and analytics, Cognyte helps customers make sense of complex, multi-source data supporting informed, mission-critical investigations and operations. Hundreds of customers worldwide rely on Cognyte’s investigative analytics solutions to uncover insights and reveal what matters, across fragmented data and organizational silos, enabling confident decision-making in high-stakes environments. Learn more at www.cognyte.com .
